topic: The first Olympic flame of the modern Games burned at the 1928 Summer Olympics in Amsterdam, in a bowl on top of the Marathon Tower of the Olympic Stadium designed by architect Jan Wils; it was lit by an employee of the Amsterdam electricity utility and served to show where the Games were. The 1896 Athens Games had no flame. Los Angeles 1932 repeated the stadium flame. The torch relay was introduced by Carl Diem for Berlin 1936: the flame was lit by the sun in Olympia on 20 July 1936 and carried 3,187 km by 3,331 runners in twelve days and eleven nights through Greece, Bulgaria, Yugoslavia, Hungary, Austria, Czechoslovakia and Germany, arriving on 1 August 1936; Leni Riefenstahl filmed it for the Nazi regime. Every Games since has held a relay from Olympia.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The Olympic flame has been lit in Greece since the first modern Games in 1896.
myths.reality: The 1896 Games had no flame; the first flame burned in Amsterdam in 1928, lit on site, and the relay from Olympia began only in 1936 for Berlin.
